chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A man enters Makkah and cuts from its trees.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Cut what has entered upon you, and do not cut what has not entered your house upon you.'

key_terms.دَاخِلًا عَلَيْكَ: Entering upon you, meaning within one's possession or domain
key_terms.شَجَرِهَا: Its trees, referring to the vegetation of Makkah
key_terms.مَنْزِلَكَ: Your house, representing one's private property or residence

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting trees in Makkah on cutting its trees according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between private ownership and the public sanctity of Makkah's vegetation, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding the Haram's boundaries. It establishes that while individuals may utilize trees within their specific domain, the general prohibition against cutting trees in the sacred precincts remains intact for those outside one's immediate property. This ruling underscores the balance between individual rights and the collective preservation of the holy site's natural resources.
